companies.label: Meituan
companies.metric_name: Core Local Commerce segment operating profit (经营溢利)
companies.metric_basis: Meituan's disclosed segment operating profit/loss for Core Local Commerce (food delivery + Keeta instant retail + in-store/hotel/travel), reported each quarter in HKEX filings

periods.src: Meituan Q3 2025 filing; Sina Finance, Tencent News

companies.latest_signal: Core local commerce swung back to a RMB5.67bn operating profit in Q2 2026 from a RMB14.1bn loss just two quarters earlier, as marketing spend discipline and easing subsidy intensity took hold; Wang Xing has publicly framed Meituan as opposed to 'involution'-style subsidy competition and pivoted commentary toward AI/long-term ecosystem investment.

companies.label: Alibaba
companies.metric_name: Taobao Tmall Group (China e-commerce) adjusted EBITA
companies.metric_basis: Alibaba does not disclose a standalone instant-commerce P&L; its proxy is Taobao Tmall Group's adjusted EBITA, whose YoY decline management explicitly attributes each call to Taobao Shangou/Ele.me instant-retail subsidy investment

periods.src: Alibaba FY26 Q4 (Jan-Mar) filing; Sina, BBT News

companies.latest_signal: CFO Toby Xu and Taobao/Tmall CEO Jiang Fan said Oct-Dec 2025 was peak instant-retail investment and per-order losses had fallen ~50% since Jul/Aug 2025; by the Apr-Jun 2026 quarter the YoY EBITA drag had eased to -30% (from -76% a year earlier) with unit economics improving every quarter and Taobao Shangou share stable near 42-45%, but group targets full instant-retail EBITA breakeven only around FY2029, so the blended metric is still down materially YoY.

companies.label: JD.com
companies.metric_name: New Businesses segment operating loss (经营亏损)
companies.metric_basis: JD's disclosed operating loss for its New Businesses segment, which has consolidated JD Takeaway (food delivery) alongside Dada, JD Property, Jingxi/Joybuy and international since Q1 2025

periods.src: JD Q2 2026 filing; 163.com, Sina, ifeng, Tencent News

companies.latest_signal: New Businesses operating loss narrowed to RMB9.85bn in Q2 2026 from RMB10.35bn in Q1 2026 and RMB14.77bn a year earlier; CFO Shan Su attributed this mainly to continued loss reduction at JD Takeaway (total delivery-related spend down >50% YoY) even as Joybuy/Jingxi investment continued on schedule.

war_summary: All three show sequentially narrowing losses through Q2 2026 after peak subsidy intensity in mid-to-late 2025 drew SAMR regulatory pressure over 'involution' (内卷式) competition and public statements from Wang Xing against share-buying via subsidies. Meituan flipped back to a core local commerce profit first and JD's New Businesses loss has nearly halved YoY, while Alibaba is still absorbing the largest sustained EBITA hit (still -30% YoY even in the latest quarter) to defend Taobao Shangou's ~42-45% instant-retail share, suggesting Alibaba has blinked least on subsidy intensity even as its narrowing pace lags the other two.
